\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Complexity.ClassPSPACE.TQBFHardParams}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Width coefficient]
\lean{Complexity.TQBFHard.wCoef}
\label{Complexity.TQBFHard.wCoef}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.W}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean symbols, and let
$d,c\in\mathbb{N}$. Write $W(N)$ for its width, $k(N)$ for its machine parameter, and
$|Q_N|$ for the number of its states. Its width coefficient is
$4dW(N)+W(N)+12k(N)d+3k(N)+2|Q_N|+8$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Bound on binary length]
\lean{Complexity.TQBFHard.wP_le}
\label{Complexity.TQBFHard.wP_le}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.wP, Complexity.LogProg.length_bits_le}
\difficulty{1}
For every natural number $n$, the length of the binary representation of $n+1$ is at
most $n+1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Encoding length bounded by width]
\lean{Complexity.TQBFHard.vlen_le_vwid}
\label{Complexity.TQBFHard.vlen_le_vwid}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.W, Complexity.Codec.wP, Complexity.TQBFHard.codeLen, Complexity.TQBFHard.vlen, Complexity.TQBFHard.vrad, Complexity.TQBFHard.vwid, Complexity.TQBFHard.wCoef, Complexity.TQBFHard.wP_le}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine over Boolean symbols, and let
$d,c$ be natural numbers. For every natural number $n$, the configuration-code length at
radius $2d(n+1)^c$ is at most the width $A(n+1)^{c+1}$, where $A$ is the coefficient
specified by the machine and $d$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Exponential bound for a linear term]
\lean{Complexity.TQBFHard.three_mul_le}
\label{Complexity.TQBFHard.three_mul_le}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $m$, $3m\le 2^{2m}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bound on the configuration count]
\lean{Complexity.TQBFHard.configBound_le_two_pow}
\label{Complexity.TQBFHard.configBound_le_two_pow}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.W, Complexity.TQBFHard.three_mul_le, Complexity.TQBFHard.vrad, Complexity.TQBFHard.vwid, Complexity.TQBFHard.wCoef, Turing.FinNDTM.configBound}
\difficulty{5}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with $k$ work tapes and state set
$S$, and let $d,c,n$ be natural numbers. Set $r=2d(n+1)^c$, $H=3(|S|+1)$, $W=H+3k+1$,
and $A=4dW+W+12kd+3k+2|S|+8$. Then $3(|S|+1)(n+2)3^{k(2r+1)}(2r+1)^k \le
2^{A(n+1)^{c+1}}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Repeated level bit pattern]
\lean{Complexity.TQBFHard.levelBits}
\label{Complexity.TQBFHard.levelBits}
\leanok
Let $w,r\in\mathbb{N}$. The level bit list consists of $r$ repetitions of a block of $w$
true bits followed by $2w$ false bits.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Quantifier bits match level bits]
\lean{Complexity.TQBFHard.map_quantBit_levelQuants}
\label{Complexity.TQBFHard.map_quantBit_levelQuants}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.QBF.quantBit, Complexity.TQBFHard.levelBits, Complexity.TQBFHard.levelQuants}
\difficulty{4}
For natural numbers $w$ and $r$, replace each existential quantifier in the level
quantifier list of width $w$ and depth $r$ by true and each universal quantifier by
false. The resulting bit list is exactly the level bit list of width $w$ and depth $r$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[All-false output list]
\lean{Complexity.TQBFHard.zeroes}
\label{Complexity.TQBFHard.zeroes}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.transduce}
For any Boolean list $l$, define its zero list to be the Boolean list of the same length
whose entries are all false.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Output of the zero transducer]
\lean{Complexity.TQBFHard.zeroes_eq}
\label{Complexity.TQBFHard.zeroes_eq}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.TQBFHard.zeroes, Complexity.transduce}
\difficulty{4}
For every finite bit string $l$, the transducer that emits false on each input bit
outputs a string consisting of exactly $l.length$ false bits.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Decoded lower-bound step]
\lean{Complexity.TQBFHard.lbStep}
\label{Complexity.TQBFHard.lbStep}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD, Turing.pairEncode}
Let $s$ be a Boolean list. Its lower-bound step is the pair encoding of the first
component decoded from $s$ and the tail obtained by dropping the first entry of the
second component decoded from $s$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Paired Boolean list chunk]
\lean{Complexity.TQBFHard.lbChunk}
\label{Complexity.TQBFHard.lbChunk}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.TQBFHard.zeroes, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD}
For a Boolean list $s$, let $f$ and $g$ be its paired first- and second-component lists,
and let $0_f$ be the zero list associated with $f$. The chunk of $s$ is empty if $g$ is
empty; otherwise it is the concatenation of $f$ with two copies of $0_f$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Length bound for the suffix step]
\lean{Complexity.TQBFHard.length_lbStep}
\label{Complexity.TQBFHard.length_lbStep}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.TQBFHard.lbStep, Complexity.length_pairEncode_drop_le}
\difficulty{1}
For every finite bit string $s$, the length of its suffix step is at most the larger of
$|s|$ and $2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Iteration of the suffix step]
\lean{Complexity.TQBFHard.lbStep_iterate}
\label{Complexity.TQBFHard.lbStep_iterate}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.TQBFHard.lbStep, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{4}
For bit strings $u$ and $v$ and a natural number $i$, applying the suffix step $i$ times
to the encoding of $(u,v)$ yields the encoding of $(u,v')$, where $v'$ is obtained by
deleting the first $i$ bits of $v$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial-time computability of level bits]
\lean{Complexity.TQBFHard.polyTimeComputable_levelBits}
\label{Complexity.TQBFHard.polyTimeComputable_levelBits}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.BlockLoop.polyTimeComputable_of_loop, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.append, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.comp, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.pairEncode, Complexity.TQBFHard.lbChunk, Complexity.TQBFHard.lbStep, Complexity.TQBFHard.lbStep_iterate, Complexity.TQBFHard.length_lbStep, Complexity.TQBFHard.levelBits, Complexity.TQBFHard.zeroes, Complexity.TQBFHard.zeroes_eq, Complexity.pairFstD_pairEncode, Complexity.pairSndD, Complexity.pairSndD_pairEncode, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_const, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_isNil, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_ite, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_pairFstD, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_pairSndD, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_tail, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_transduce, Turing.length_pairEncode, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{6}
Let $w$ assign a natural number to each finite Boolean string. If the function sending a
string $x$ to the string of $w(x)$ true bits is computable in polynomial time, then the
function sending $x$ to the concatenation of $w(x)$ copies of a block consisting of
$w(x)$ true bits followed by $2w(x)$ false bits is computable in polynomial time.
\end{theorem}
